claims.text: The development of a protective oxide layer in high-entropy alloys is governed by Cr and Ta content.
The retention of a protective oxide layer in high-entropy alloys is governed by Cr and Ta content.
Cr and Ta promote formation of a stable, adherent oxide layer.
A stable, adherent oxide layer provides oxidation resistance.
The presence and concentration of Cr and Ta in the oxide layer are the proposed structural mediator.
Cr and Ta content influences the thermodynamic stability of the oxide layer.
Cr and Ta content influences the kinetic growth rate of the oxide layer.
Changes in oxide-layer thermodynamic stability and growth kinetics lead to formation of a protective oxide layer.
HEAs with higher Cr and Ta content will have lower oxidation rates than HEAs with lower Cr and Ta content.
HEAs with higher Cr and Ta content will retain their protective oxide layers better than HEAs with lower Cr and Ta content.
The beneficial effect of Cr and Ta is expected to be most pronounced above 800 degrees Celsius.
The beneficial effect of Cr and Ta may be less significant at lower temperatures.
A controlled comparison should vary Cr and Ta content among multiple HEA compositions under high-temperature exposure.
The comparison should measure oxidation rate, oxide-layer thickness and composition, and oxide/alloy microstructure.
The hypothesis would be falsified if oxidation resistance were independent of Cr and Ta content.
The hypothesis would be falsified if adding Cr and Ta degraded oxidation resistance.
